annotations.annotation_text: Page 47 opens Book 1, Chapter 2 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe, featuring HCE, the Cad, Hosty. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 47 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind

annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "Earwicker" on page 47 within "The Encounter in Phoenix Park": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. During this Age of Gods phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
